In the [[representation theory]] of [[semisimple Lie algebra]]s, '''Category O''' (or '''category <math>\mathcal{O}</math>''') is a [[category (mathematics)|category]] whose objects are certain [[Lie algebra representation|representations]] of a [[semisimple Lie algebra]], and whose morphisms are homomorphisms of representations.

== Introduction ==
Assume that <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> is a (usually [[complex number|complex]]) semisimple Lie algebra with a [[Cartan subalgebra]] <math>\mathfrak{h}</math>. Let <math>\Phi</math> be its [[root system]] and let <math>\Phi^+</math> be a choice of [[root system#Positive roots and simple roots|positive roots]]. Denote by <math>\mathfrak{g}_\alpha</math> the [[root space]] corresponding to a root <math>\alpha\in\Phi</math>, and set
<math>\mathfrak{n}:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\mathfrak{g}_\alpha</math>,
a [[nilpotent Lie algebra|nilpotent]] subalgebra.

If <math>M</math> is a <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>-module and <math>\lambda\in\mathfrak{h}^*</math>, then the <math>\lambda</math>-[[Weight (representation theory)#Weight space of a representation|weight space]] of <math>M</math> is
:<math>M_\lambda=\{v\in M:\forall h\in\mathfrak{h},\; h\cdot v=\lambda(h)v\}.</math>

== Definition of category O ==
The objects of category <math>\mathcal O</math> are <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>-modules <math>M</math> such that:
# <math>M</math> is finitely generated;
# <math>M=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{h}^*} M_\lambda</math>;
# <math>M</math> is locally <math>\mathfrak{n}</math>-finite, i.e. for each <math>v\in M</math>, the <math>\mathfrak{n}</math>-submodule generated by <math>v</math> is finite-dimensional.

Morphisms in this category are the <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>-module homomorphisms.

== Basic properties ==
{{Expand section|date=September 2011}}
* Each module in category <math>\mathcal O</math> has finite-dimensional weight spaces.
* Each module in category <math>\mathcal O</math> is a [[Noetherian module]].
* <math>\mathcal O</math> is an [[abelian category]].
* <math>\mathcal O</math> has [[projective object|enough projectives]] and [[injective object|enough injectives]].
* <math>\mathcal O</math> is closed under taking [[submodule]]s, quotients, and finite direct sums.
* Objects in <math>\mathcal O</math> are <math>Z(\mathfrak{g})</math>-finite: if <math>M</math> is an object and <math>v\in M</math>, then the subspace <math>Z(\mathfrak{g})v\subseteq M</math> generated by <math>v</math> under the action of the [[center (algebra)|center]] of the [[universal enveloping algebra]] is finite-dimensional.

== Koszul duality ==
A homological feature of category <math>\mathcal O</math> is that, after choosing graded lifts of blocks, certain blocks can be described by [[Koszul algebra]]s. In particular, Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel showed that (for suitable graded realizations) the endomorphism algebra of a projective generator of a block (notably the principal block) is a Koszul algebra <math>A</math>.<ref name="BGS1996">{{Cite journal
 | last1 = Beilinson
 | first1 = Alexander
 | last2 = Ginzburg
 | first2 = Victor
 | last3 = Soergel
 | first3 = Wolfgang
 | title = Koszul duality patterns in representation theory
 | journal = Journal of the American Mathematical Society
 | volume = 9
 | year = 1996
 | pages = 473–527
}}</ref>
Equivalently, the corresponding graded block of <math>\mathcal O</math> is (via a projective generator) equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional graded modules over <math>A</math>.

In this setting, Koszul duality relates two graded blocks: one block is equivalent to <math>\mathrm{gr}\text{-}A</math>, while a second (dual) graded block is equivalent to <math>\mathrm{gr}\text{-}A^{!}</math>, where <math>A^{!}</math> is the Koszul dual algebra of <math>A</math>.<ref name="BGS1996" />
The associated Koszul duality functors induce a triangulated equivalence between the bounded derived categories of these graded realizations, i.e. an equivalence of the form
:<math>D^{b}(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{block}}^{\mathrm{gr}})\;\simeq\;D^{b}(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{block}^\vee}^{\mathrm{gr}}),</math>
where <math>\mathcal O_{\mathrm{block}}^{\mathrm{gr}}\simeq \mathrm{gr}\text{-}A</math> and <math>\mathcal O_{\mathrm{block}^\vee}^{\mathrm{gr}}\simeq \mathrm{gr}\text{-}A^{!}</math>.<ref name="BGS1996" />

Koszul duality for category <math>\mathcal O</math> is closely connected with geometric and combinatorial structures such as the geometry of the flag variety, [[perverse sheaves]], and [[Kazhdan–Lusztig theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal
 | last = Soergel
 | first = Wolfgang
 | title = Kategorie O, perverse Garben und Moduln über den Koinvarianten zur Weylgruppe
 | journal = Journal of the American Mathematical Society
 | volume = 3
 | year = 1990
 | pages = 421–445
}}</ref>

== Examples ==
{{Expand section|date=September 2011}}
* All finite-dimensional <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>-modules and their <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>-homomorphisms are in category <math>\mathcal O</math>.
* [[Verma module]]s and [[generalized Verma module]]s and their <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>-homomorphisms are in category <math>\mathcal O</math>.
